Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
708 AM EST Sun Nov 8 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 138 AM EST Sunday...

No significant changes were made with this forecast update.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 200 AM EST Sunday...

1. Cooler and unsettled weather will persist through the first 
half of this week with rounds of showers expected. 

2. Unsettled weather continues through the end of the week, 
likely trending cooler by next weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 138 AM EST Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Precipitation will continue to slowly wind down through 
the early morning hours as an upper level low pinwheels away to the 
east. While most of the precipitation is falling as rain or drizzle, 
temperatures in the higher elevations and portions of the Northeast 
Kingdom are in the low to mid 30s; our sensor on Mt Mansfield at 
just short of 4000 ft is reading 28F as of 1 am. Therefore expect 
these areas are seeing periods of snow, though ground temperatures 
should be warm enough to preclude any accumulation below 2500 ft. 
Cameras on some of the higher elevation roads in the Northeast 
Kingdom courtesy of VTrans do appear to show a bit of snow 
falling with no accumulation noted, though it's difficult to 
discern for sure due to darkness and thick fog. These lingering 
showers will taper to an end by mid to late morning or so, 
allowing for a dry Sunday afternoon. Highs will be in the low 
40s to low 50s, with a bit of a brisk wind at 5 to 15 mph with 
local gusts to around 20 mph. 

Additional rounds of showers are expected then through the first 
half of this week as we remain under the influence of a large upper 
level low gyrating over eastern Canada. Multiple shortwaves rotating 
around the base of this low will pivot overhead, keeping the weather 
unsettled over the next few days. Much like our current system, much 
of the shower activity will fall as rain, especially during the 
daylight hours, but some snow will be possible across the higher 
terrain and portions of the Adirondacks/Northeast Kingdom, 
especially overnight. Any accumulation will be minimal below 2500 
ft, but we'll be watching closely to see if Mt Mansfield is able to 
break the record for latest 1" of snowfall (Nov 9). Highs will be in 
the low/mid 40s to low 50s each day, with lows falling into the 
upper 20s to mid/upper 30s. Winds will remain on the breezy side, 
but not strong enough to cause any significant impacts.

KEY MESSAGE 2: The large Hudson Bay low will continue to dominate the 
weather across our area, bringing multiple shortwaves into region 
through the weekend. Wednesday should see lingering, terrain driven 
mix of rain and snow showers throughout the day. Models on Thursday 
remain torn on the timing and placement of warm front ahead of the 
developing low in the Ohio Valley. The solutions could bring a rain-
snow mix, or keep things further south and keep our area relatively 
dry during the day. For Friday and the weekend, models are still 
keying in on significant closed low swinging down through the Mid-
Atlantic region and then up the coastline, bringing several shots of 
rain and rain/snow mix over the weekend. The current runs are 
leaning towards a wetter solution for our region which could bring 
the first significant snow of the season. The details should come 
into better focus over the next few days.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Through 12Z Monday...Low ceilings, rain, and mist continue to
start the period, with MVFR, IFR, and LIFR conditions currently.
Showers will scatter out and ceilings will slowly lift after 
14Z. However, improvement will be slow, especially at higher 
elevation TAF sites where IFR conditions could persist into the 
early afternoon. By late afternoon and evening Sunday, ceilings 
areawide will lift to MVFR/VFR levels. 

Winds will remain from the north generally 6-12 knots, with some
occasional gusts 15 to 18 knots this afternoon. 

Outlook...

Monday: MVFR. Chance SHRA.
Monday Night: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Tuesday: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Tuesday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Veterans Day: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Wednesday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Thursday: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. NO SIG WX.

&&

VT...None.
NY...None.
